Structural outlook · 2030 horizon
Where does pressure build if today's trends hold?
Not a prediction. Each 2030 figure is today's structural score, rescored with the import dependence that population growth and the food-output trend imply by 2030. Nothing else moves.
▸ How this is computed
Each 2030 number = today's structural score rescored with import dependence moved by 100 × (n₂₀₃₀ − n), where n = net imports ÷ staple use (FAOSTAT 2024, USDA) and n₂₀₃₀ = 1 − (1 − n)((1 + r)/(1 + g))⁶, g = World Bank population growth, r = FAOSTAT food-output trend 2015–24. Countries missing any of the three inputs show no change and say so. It is not an econometric forecast of where each country will actually be in 2030: and no formal back-test pipeline exists yet (it's on the roadmap). Layer shocks on top in the Scenario Stress Test; see the Methodology page for inputs.

Third-party claims, not measured data: how to read this page
Each headline below is a claim by its publisher; we link, we do not verify. Commodity and country attribution are modeled: our keyword match on the headline. Corridor tonnages are sourced from the bilateral trade atlas. A headline touching a corridor is not a claim that it moves prices.
Most reached right now
Ranked by how many current headlines touch a corridor into that country. Volume is the largest single corridor touched: not a sum, because adding wheat to palm oil gives a number that means nothing.

Live Disturbances
Hazard alerts, crisis classifications and supply shocks, rebuilt every six hours from GDACS, ReliefWeb, IPC/CH (via WFP), FEWS NET (28 countries), Open-Meteo weather and river flow, USGS gauges, IMF PortWatch and FX rates. Curated baseline events are marked BASELINE; wire headlines are marked CLAIM.
About FoodShield AI · Built in Rotterdam
Which countries run short of food first when a shock hits, and why.
When one country fails tomorrow (a war, a drought, a port closure), FoodShield shows who gets hurt, and how badly. Built by one student at Erasmus University Rotterdam, it combines 67 public data sources into one comparable score per country: — refreshed automatically and — curated by hand. Each input links to its source.
Open Methodology · dated from the data manifest
The score, its weights and its inputs, on one page.
The Food Disruption Risk Score is one 0–100 composite per country, built from nine components drawn from public data. The score on a country page is that composite plus a bounded live adjustment. The weights, the inputs and the formula are below, so any score can be recomputed by hand.
Built from · FAO· USDA PSD· World Bank· IMF· IPC· FEWS NET· HDX HAPI (ACLED)· ND-GAIN· INFORM· UN Comtrade
Companies · researched majors · cited claims from their own filings
Where eleven major food and fertilizer companies say they source, in their own filings.
Eleven traders and fertilizer producers, Cargill, ADM, Bunge, Wilmar, Olam, LDC, JBS, Tyson, COFCO, Nutrien and Yara, each with a country list taken from their own annual reports, ESG reports and filings: 222 cited claims across 44 countries. Only Nutrien’s file is fully verified; the rest are provisional. Viterra, part of Bunge since July 2025, is kept as a pre-merger record and is searchable. Mosaic, OCP, CF Industries, EuroChem, WH Group and CP Group are not covered yet. Below the majors, other firms are listed by commodity overlap: inferred, not disclosed.
Sources · Annual reports· ESG / sustainability reports· SEC / HKEX / OSE filings· Asset-location pages
▸ ● What's sourced vs modeled · what we can't get
Sourced: Country lists for the 12 majors are drawn from each company's own published material: annual reports, ESG / sustainability reports, asset-location pages, SEC / HKEX / OSE filings. Each listed country links to the filing it came from.
Modeled fallback: Less-disclosed regional players use a commodity-overlap heuristic (their known commodities × importer/exporter countries). Labeled in the UI.
What we can't get: Tonnage or share-of-volume per country, no trader publishes this. The Sourced Exposure score weights each country equally, useful as a directional risk-screen, not a quantitative supply-chain weight.

Privacy & cookies
What this site does and does not collect. Last reviewed 26 September 2026.

This site sets no cookies. Nothing is written to document.cookie anywhere in the application, so there is no consent banner because there is nothing to consent to.

What is stored on your device

Four values in your browser's localStorage, which never leave your device and are not readable by anyone else:

  • foodshield_skip_intro: whether you ticked "don't show again" on the welcome panel
  • foodshield_hint_shown: whether you have seen the first-visit map hint
  • fs-rail-collapsed: whether you collapsed the side rail
  • fs_signups: a local copy of any email address you submit to the updates form, kept so the form can tell it has already been sent

Clearing your browser's site data for this domain removes all four.

Analytics

Vercel Web Analytics, loaded from this site's own domain at /_vercel/insights. It is cookieless and records aggregate page views and referrers. It does not build a profile of you, does not follow you to other sites, and is not used for advertising.

If you submit your email

The updates form is the only place this site asks for personal data, and it is optional. A submitted address is sent to Formspree (formspree.io), a third-party form processor, and is also kept in localStorage as described above. It is used to send occasional updates about this project and nothing else: it is not sold, rented or passed to advertisers. To have an address removed, email the address in the footer.

If you use Ask FoodShield

A question you type into Ask FoodShield is sent, with the page's figures for the countries and crops it names, to this site's own server and from there to Anthropic's API, which writes the answer. Where that is not configured, the site's server sends the same question and figures to Pollinations (pollinations.ai), a free open-model service, instead. The question and answer are not stored by this site and are not linked to you; Anthropic processes them under its commercial terms and does not train its models on API traffic. Do not type personal information into the box. The data packet sent with each question can be read under "Data sent with this question" beneath the answer.

Third parties your browser contacts

Loading the dashboard fetches assets and map tiles from other hosts. Those hosts necessarily see your IP address and browser, in the ordinary way any website request does:

  • OpenFreeMap and CARTO: vector map tiles, requested as you pan and zoom
  • jsDelivr: the MapLibre map library and the Natural Earth boundary files
  • Google Fonts: the typefaces
  • GDACS: hazard alerts, only as a fallback if the server-side snapshot is unavailable

Each of those is a separate organisation with its own privacy policy. This site sends them no information about you beyond the request itself.

What this site does not do

No accounts, no logins, no advertising, no ad networks, no cross-site trackers, no fingerprinting, no sale or sharing of personal data. The dashboard's underlying data is public, and the source code is on GitHub.
